INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The Arts Commission meeting was held on Wednesday, September 15, 2021 via Zoom. Commissioner Metcalf called the
meeting to order at 6:33 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District 1
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District 2
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District 3
  Commissioner Vicki Banks, District 4
  Sabrina Barnes, Director, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Battle made a motion to approve the minutes from July 21, 2021. Commissioner Lesure seconded
and the minutes were approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners Lessure, Metcalf, Ehrlich-Bell and Banks
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

Helen Lessick gave verbal reports regarding the following Public Art related projects:

    Rogers Park Artist in Residence, Shelley Heffler and Delis Frank invited all to participate in the It Takes a Village:
  Inglewood Fine Art Quilting Workshops where they will provide instruction in quilting 12” fabric squares, as part of
  her participatory public art project to be on display in January 2022 at Rogers Park Community Center. Ms. Heffler
  recognizes that it takes a village to celebrate community warmth and beauty through art. Workshops will run from
  September 17, 2021 to December 18, 2021.Separate workshops for youth and adults; classes capped at 12
  participants. All skill levels welcome; masks required; pandemic protocol will be observed.
    Inglewood Arts and Culture Walking Tour Series: This is a community engagement and educational project looking
  to debut in January/February 2022 during Super Bowl festivities and will consist of six one-hour mapped tours,
  arranged by proximity to highlight public art, architecture and engaging attractions throughout the City including the
  Civic Center area and Downtown Market Street. Additional images are being gathered to include the sports and
  entertainment series, the Crenshaw Corridor, Gardens and Parks and finally the neighborhood series. More
  1

  ARTS COMMISSION

  information can be found at www.inglewoodpublicart.org/about. Commissioner Lesure asked are these up and
  currently running, are they accessible. Ms. Lessick stated the Civic Center is up and the remainder are in progress.
    Inglewood Growing Artists Project (IGAP) 2022: Planning is underway for the next IGAP project and staff would like
  the Commission’s input on an art project or an art experience. Commissioner Lesure asked if this for one (1) artist or
  can it be divided between a few artists. Director Barnes stated there are $25,000 and we can elect to split it but it
  would mean a smaller project. Commissioner Metcalf stated the notional timeline discussed at the last meeting, on
  the disbursement of funds seemed very reasonable. Director Barnes gave clarification on funds specific to the $2
  million dollars that Hollywood Park is going to spend as a part of their own projects. This money here is from our
  Public Art fund. Commissioner Metcalf looks forward to hearing staff’s suggestions.
    Beckman YOLA Center Grand Opening: The August 15th grand opening was canceled due to COVID-19 however,
  the facility is open and students are onsite. Anyone interested in classes can register at www.LAPHIL.ORG/YOLA.
  The center is receiving international attention. Those who may be interested in teaching opportunities should
  monitor the website. The Center is really interested in hiring residents of Inglewood.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners’ Comments/Initiatives/Art Calendar

  Helen Lessick shared the cover story of ARTFORUM, a publication out of New York. The article is about
Inglewood’s Residency Art Gallery and the Crenshaw Diary Mart. Inglewood is in the international news and it’s really
important for us to take pride.

  Commissioner Battle stated she visited the YOLA Center and it is really a beautiful building. She spoke with the
Director about some ideas and is ecstatic about the building. The acoustics are beautiful and looks forward to being
involved.

  Commissioner Banks thanked staff for the presentation.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:14 p.m.
